author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Markets have declared the Fed's hiking cycle over: a bull flattening that took 61 bps off the 10Y and 43 bps off the 2Y in 20 observations, a DXY down 3.65% and a VIX at 12.98 have lifted every rate-sensitive asset even as Q3 GDP was revised up to 5.2% and holiday spending gains softened. The opportunity is in assets that benefit from easier dollar liquidity (duration, quality growth, semis, EM dollar debt, Polish banks via dollar returns), while China beta, energy and state-controlled Polish names such as Orlen carry the policy risk the rally is ignoring.
sources_policy: Only the frozen 2023-11-30 feed (via tools/digest.py) and the 2023-11-30 market card (via tools/showcard.py) were used; exclusions/2023-11-30.json ids were not cited. Every concrete fact is attributed to a headline cited in the same paragraph or to the card; numbers are card values or appear in a same-paragraph cited headline; pending events (China PMI, OPEC+ decision, Cybertruck delivery event, bitcoin ETF decision, Polish government handover) are described only as pending, with no outcomes. No spot-FX levels or returns are quoted; currency direction comes from dated headlines. Records whose event plausibly post-dates 00:00 UTC on 2023-11-30 were not used.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0221 (Reuters, 'China's factories fall deeper into contraction, more policy support expected', dated 2023-11-29 08:00): describes the official November PMI released about 01:30 UTC on 2023-11-30, after the cutoff; misdated, same event as excluded n0223. Recommend exclusion.

n1037 (Retail Dive, 'Foot Locker beats expectations, but sales continue to tumble', dated 2023-11-29): Foot Locker's Q3 results are not plausibly before the cutoff (reported in early December); treated as misdated. Recommend exclusion.

n1735 (Reuters POLL 'Economic risks to stifle oil's gains in 2024 despite OPEC+ cuts', dated 2023-11-29): Reuters' monthly oil poll is normally published on the month's last business day (2023-11-30); release likely after the cutoff. Not used; recommend exclusion.

n0220 (Reuters, 'China new home prices now seen climbing this year after policy steps', dated 2023-11-29, monthly category): Reuters property poll whose publication date relative to the cutoff could not be established from the headline; not used.
n0724 (Barron's, Costco's November sales): Costco's November sales release date relative to the cutoff could not be established; not used.
n0801 (Reuters, Occidental in talks to buy CrownRock): timing of the report relative to the cutoff uncertain; not used.
n0839 (Disney board appoints Gorman and Darroch): announcement may post-date the cutoff; not used.
n0088 (Reuters, 'Dollar rises from 3-1/2-month low; rate cut bets intact'): could be a 2023-11-30 Asian-session report; not used (n1906 and n1131 used for dollar direction instead).
n0765 / n1040 (Hormel Q4 results): release date relative to the cutoff not certain from headlines; not used.

n0603 (Bloomberg, 'Micron Falls Despite Raising Earnings Outlook, Beating Estimates', dated 2023-11-28): describes a reported quarter beat that does not match a late-November event; treated as likely misdated, not used.
n1725 (The Economist, 'An unruly OPEC is causing problems for Russia and Saudi Arabia', dated 2023-11-29): weekly-edition article whose online release may fall on 2023-11-30; not used.
n0712 (thebull.com.au, CSL trading near three-year lows): stale relative to CSL's card close and 20-session gain; not used.
n0484 / n0789 (MediaTek or Taiwan tech stock up 40%): horizon and timing of the move unclear; not used.
n0144 / n0145 (GameStop retail rally): left to the retail section to avoid citation-count collisions.
